rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samk is the sky's height above the earth toward the upper direction; it may also mean thickness, whose upper-to-lower measure is called depth.
rows.anchor: جعل مقدار ارتفاعها من الأرض وذهابها إلى سمت العلو مديدا رفيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound reports give five hundred years of travel between earth and the lowest heaven, and likewise between heavens and for each heaven's thickness; he takes the measure literally as customary travel and a definite number.
rows.anchor: جاء في الأخبار الصحيحة أن ارتفاع السماء الدنيا عن الأرض خمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the heaven even in accordance with wisdom, leaving no part without what its wisdom requires, including adornment with stars.
rows.anchor: جعلها سواء فيما اقتضته الحكمة فلم يخل عز وجل قطعة منها عما تقتضيه الحكمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation takes making it even to mean smoothing its surface so it has no rises or depressions.
rows.anchor: وقيل تسويتها جعلها ملساء ليس في سطحها انخفاض وارتفاع

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Another view says the heavens have simple, similar parts and a genuinely spherical form; many scholars held this, citing their created dependence on a freely choosing maker and seeing no religious harm in sphericity.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب كثير وقالوا وحكاه الإمام لما ثبت أنها محدثة مفتقرة إلى فاعل مختار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view reads the phrase as completing the heavens with stars, celestial accessories, and epicycles; al-Alusi says this rests on an early-unattested identification of heavens with spheres and on weak astronomical proofs, so the truth is left to God.
rows.anchor: هذا مع بنائه على اتحاد السماوات والأفلاك غير معروف في الصدر الأول من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought out the earth's water by opening springs and causing rivers to flow.
rows.anchor: بأن فجر منها عيونا وأجرى أنهارا ومرعاها يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marʿā can mean pasture or fodder, grazing as a verbal noun, or a place or time; although some make place its original sense, fodder best fits this context.
rows.anchor: يقع على الرعي بالكسر وهو الكلأ والرعي بالفتح وهو المصدر وكذا على الموضع والزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict pasture to what animals eat and extend it to human food by metonymy; al-Tibi allows an explicit metaphor, addressing resurrection-deniers as people yoked with beasts in worldly enjoyment and heedlessness of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال الطيبي يجوز أن يكون استعارة مصرحة لأن الكلام مع منكري الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase explains and completes the earth's spreading: settlement requires provision for livelihood, including food and drink; syntactically it can also be a circumstantial clause with an implicit qad, either way without a conjunction.
rows.anchor: بيان وتفسير لدحاها وتكملة له فإن السكنى لا تتأتى بمجرد البسط

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One analysis makes mataʿan an object of purpose: God did these things to provide enjoyment for people and their livestock, who benefit from the water and pasture.
rows.anchor: قيل مفعول له أي فعل ذلك تدمتيعا لكم ولأنعامكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively it is an emphatic verbal noun for an omitted verb, or a verbal noun with different wording because the preceding actions mean providing enjoyment.
rows.anchor: وقيل مصدر مؤكد لفعله المضمر أي متعكم بذلك متاعا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An objection to the purpose analysis is that the address targets resurrection-deniers whereas the intended beneficiaries are believers; the author replies that direct address is limited to those present but its ruling generalizes to humankind.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن خطاب المشافهة وإن كان خاصا بالحاضرين إلا أن حكمه عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the word a verbal noun through an implied verb does not remove the objection, since it still introduces a statement of purpose; moreover, the claim that only believers are intended beneficiaries is debatable.
rows.anchor: وأيضا النصب على المصدرية بفعله المقدر لا يدفع المحذور لكونه استئنافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to direct address reassures the Prophet after the preceding rebuke, replacing estrangement with attention and turning toward him after turning away.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من الإيناس بعد الإيحاش والإقبال بعد الإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Ibn Umm Maktum the blind man highlights his excuse for interrupting the Prophet's speech while he was occupied with the people, and invites compassion toward him.
rows.anchor: للأشعار بعذره في الإقدام على قطع كلام الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation sees the initial third-person wording followed by direct address as heightened censure, like publicly complaining and then confronting the offender with blame and proof.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الغيبة أولا والخطاب ثانيا لزيادة الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description also hints that every weak person deserves the consideration shown to someone in his condition, rather than restricting the lesson to this particular blind man.
rows.anchor: وفيه أيضا دفع إيهام الإختصاص بالأعمى المعين وإيماء إلى أن كل ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an elided causal lām, the phrase modifies the first verb for Kufans, the second for Basrans, and both for al-Farra; all agree it gives the cause of both actions in meaning.
rows.anchor: وهو معمول لأول الفعلين على مختار الكوفيين وثانيهما على مختار البصريين

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads ʿabasa with a doubled bāʾ for intensification, not to make the form causative.
rows.anchor: قرأ زيد بن علي على عبس بتشديد الباء للمبالغة لا للتعدية

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمران الجوني وعيسى وبعض القراء
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Imran al-Jawni, and Isa read with one hamza, while some readers use two articulated hamzas; in both readings the hamza is an interrogative of repudiation.
rows.anchor: والحسن وأبو عمران الجوني وعيسى آن بهمزة بعدها وبعض القراء بهمزتين محققتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pause is made at tawalla, and the sense is an elliptical exception: except that the blind man came, then the rebuke is directed accordingly.
rows.anchor: والهمزة في القراءتين للأستفهام الأنكاري ويوقف على تولي والمعنى إلا أن جاء الأعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in laʿallahu refers to the blind man, and the clause appears to attach to the verb of knowing as its object: what could make you know that he may purify himself?
rows.anchor: وضمير لعله للأعمى والظاهر أن الجملة متعلقة بفعل الدراية على وجه سد مسد مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification here is his cleansing himself of some traces of sin through the religious teachings he learns.
rows.anchor: أي أي شيء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى لعله يتطهر بما يتلقن من الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhdhakkaru means that he takes admonition; the reminder that benefits him is the Prophet's exhortation and preaching.
rows.anchor: أو يذكر أي يتعظ فتنفعه الذكرى أي ذكراك وموعظتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not know whether the man would purify himself or remember; the verse denies such foreknowledge, since knowing the outcome would have prevented what happened.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنك لا تدري ما هو مترقب منه من ترك أو تذكر ولو دريت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The hope may belong to the blind man or to the Prophet; even a reasonable hope that he would purify himself was enough to forbid frowning and turning away, especially given his demonstrated receptiveness.
rows.anchor: والترجي راجع إلى الأعمى أو إلى النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purification is treated as something hoped for rather than certain, so the term can denote some purification rather than complete purification; the wording gives the basic sense without requiring perfection.
rows.anchor: اعتبر متعلق التزكي بعض الأوضار ترشيحا لذلك وفيه إظهار ما يقتضي مقام العظمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take the omitted object of ma yudrika to be the man's affair and final state; the following clause then resumes and explains the hint that he has an important, divinely known prospect.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم متعلق الدراية محذوف أي ما يدريك أمره وعاقبة حاله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On that analysis purification can mean total cleansing from sin, while remembering can benefit him if he does not attain complete purification; the author calls a further proposed distinction between obligatory and optional learning weak.
rows.anchor: أي لعله يتطهر بما يقتبس منك من أوضار الأثم بالكلية أو يتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage indirectly suggests that the disbelievers receiving the Prophet's attention were not expected to purify themselves, as in telling a poor learner that perhaps another, capable listener will understand.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تعريض وإشعار بأن من تصدى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لتزكيتهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says the alluded person was already purified from sins and receptive to admonition.
rows.anchor: وقيل جاء التعريض من جهة أن المحدث عنه كان متزكيا من الآثام متعظا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some make the pronoun refer to the disbeliever, with hope attributed to the Prophet, who hoped for his conversion and so turned from the blind man; al-Alusi rejects this because the disbeliever was not previously mentioned and the pronoun is singular despite the group addressed, though a report says the person was one.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضمير لعله للكافر والترجي راجع إلى الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الأعرج وعاصم في رواية
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj and one transmission from Asim read yadhdhakkaru with a still dhāl and a damma on kāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج وعاصم في رواية أو يذكر بسكون الذال وضم الكاف

rows.speaker: الأكثر وعاصم والأعرج وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة والزعفراني
rows.claim: Most readers raise tanfaʿuhu by coordination with yadhdhakkaru; Asim in the common reading, al-Aʿraj, Abu Haywa, Ibn Abi Abla, and al-Zaʿfarani read it in the accusative, supplied by an implied an for Basrans or as the response to hope for Kufans.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأكثر فتنفعه بالرفع عطفا على يذكر وبالنصب قرأ عاصم في المشهور

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the accusative reading favors taking the pronoun as the disbeliever, since hope then approaches a wish for an unlikely outcome; under the prior interpretation, the reading can instead reinforce the sense of qualified, incomplete purification.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف أن النصب يؤيد رجوع ضمير لعله على الكافر لا شمام الترجي معنى التمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet bears no blame if the disbeliever does not purify himself; eagerness for his conversion should not cause the Prophet to turn away from someone who has believed.
rows.anchor: وليس عليك بأس في أن لا يزكى بالأسلام حتى يبعثك الحرص على إسلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma is negative and the clause is circumstantial from the subject of taṣaddā; alternatively it is an interrogative repudiation meaning the same thing: what harm is it if he does not purify himself?
rows.anchor: فما نافية والجملة حال من ضمير تصدى والممنوع عنه في الحقيقة الأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He comes hastening, seeking from the Prophet guidance's rulings and qualities of good.
rows.anchor: أي حال كونه مسرعا طالبا لما عندك من أحكام الرشد وخصال الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears God; alternatively he fears harm from the disbelievers when coming, or stumbling because he has no guide.
rows.anchor: أي يخاف الله تعالى وقيل أذية الكفار في الإتيان وقيل العثار والكبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause huwa yakhsha is circumstantial from the subject of yasʿā, just as yasʿā is circumstantial from the subject of jāʾaka.
rows.anchor: والجملة حال من فاعل يسعى كما أن جملة يسعى حال من فاعل جاءك

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: A scholar proposes ellipsis by ihtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies poverty later, while mentioning the poor man's coming and fear implies their opposites earlier; al-Alusi says this device is unnecessary given his prior explanation.
rows.anchor: استظهر بعض الأفاضل أن النظم الجليل من الأحتباك ذكر الغنى أو لا للدلالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the path as the newborn's way out of the womb, made easy by opening the womb, extending nerves along the passage, and turning the head downward after it had been upward.
rows.anchor: كما في رواية عن ابن عباس بأن فتح فم الرحم ومدد الأعصاب في طريقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وأبو صالح والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi explain the path as sound reflection leading to faith; God eases it by granting reason and enabling thought.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة وأبي صالح والسدي المراد بالسبيل سبيل النظر القويم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وعطاء
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Ata, with another report from Ibn Abbas, take the path to mean both guidance and error: God enables a person to follow either good or evil.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن وعطاء وهو رواية عن الحبر أيضا هو سبيل الهدى والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Facilitating both good and evil is still an evident blessing because the person is empowered for either, regardless of the moral direction chosen.
rows.anchor: والأقدار على المراد نعمة ظاهرة بقطع النظر عن خيريته وشريته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another answer counts the evil path as a blessing because one could not deserve praise and reward for turning away from it if it were not accessible like the good path; this assumes that abstention without ability is not rewarded, while another view rewards and praises one who resolves not to sin even if able.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو لم يكن مسهلا كسبيل الخير لم يستحق المدح والثواب بالأعراض عنه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say inability to do evil is itself a blessing and cite a Persian couplet thanking God for lacking the power to harm people.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم العجز عن الشر نعمة وأنشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative by an implied verb explained by the following verb, intensifying ease and reinforcing it in the mind through repetition.
rows.anchor: ونصب السبيل بمضمر يفسره الظاهر وفيه مبالغة في التيسير وتمكين في النفس بسبب التكرير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some find generality in the definite article: saying his path might suggest that each person has a path peculiar to him; some limit this observation to the guidance-and-error interpretation.
rows.anchor: قيل وفي تعريفه باللام دون الإضافة إشعار بعمومه فإنه لو قيل سبيله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On the guidance-and-error interpretation, the verse hints that worldly life is a path whose destination lies elsewhere, since the path leads to reward or punishment; al-Alusi calls this implication obscure.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا المعنى قيل إن فيه إيماء إلى أن الدنيا طريق والمقصد غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object pronoun in yassara refers to al-sabīl; the intervening material creates no ambiguity or defect in clarity.
rows.anchor: فالضمير المنصوب في يسره للسبيل وليس في التفكيك لبس حتى يكون نقصا في البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people have not fulfilled what they were commanded despite the prior blessings that call for obedience, they should consider their food, perhaps this prompts fulfillment.
rows.anchor: على معنى إذا كان هذا حال الإنسان وهو أنه إلى الآن لم يقض ما أمره

rows.speaker: العصامية
rows.claim: Al-Isami's marginal note says the rebuke that people have not fulfilled their command strongly stirs them to obey the following command to look; the transition assumes obedience follows abandoning their present course.
rows.anchor: وفي الحواشي العصامية لا يخفى ما في قوله تعالى لما يقض ما أمره من كمال تهييج الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent is humankind generally, as in the earlier statement 'man is destroyed'; al-Isami allows a universal failure to fulfill, with the commanded observer distinct from the disbelieving human meant by the failure.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالإنسان هنا نحو ما أريد به في قوله تعالى قتل الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion contrasts blessings inherent to the human self and its needs with external blessings; proposed alternatives call the first special and second general, or the first about coming into being and second about continued life, the latter distinction being questionable.
rows.anchor: نعم الذاتية أي ما يتعلق بذات الإنسان من الذات نفسها ولوازمها وهذا ذكر النعم الخارجية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food means consumables of every kind; drink is omitted because food displays more signs of divine power, while explaining the omission by subsuming drink is unconvincing.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالطعام المطعوم بأنواعه واقتصر عليه ولم يذكر المشروب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God split the earth with plants in a wondrous way fitted to each plant's size, shape, form, and appearance.
rows.anchor: أي بالنبات كما قال ابن عباس شقا بديعا لائقا بما يشقها من النبات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the splitting to mean plowing; attributing it to God is figurative attribution to the cause, though God is the true creator, but the author notes that thumma counts against this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل شقها بالكراب وإسناده إلى ضميره تعالى مجاز من باب الإسناد إلى السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An action is properly attributed to the agent in whom it subsists, not to the one who produces it in another; this is why the agent's active participle is derived from it.
rows.anchor: أن إسناد الفعل حقيقة لمن قام به لا من صدر عنه إيجادا ولهذا يشتق اسم الفاعل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ is suitable if splitting means plant growth through the stage when grain forms: the splitting progressively widens, so grain follows it; intervening human plowing would disrupt the passage's account of divine gifts.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد بالنبات ما نبت من الأرض إلى أن يتكامل وينعقد الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grain means the generic edible, storable crops such as wheat, barley, and maize.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالحب جنس الحبوب التي يتقوت بها وتدخر كالحنطة والشعير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A defense of the plowing interpretation says the conjunction need not make every limitation of the first action apply to the second; plowing may be illustrative or may mean digging, since it does not suit grapes, olives, and palms.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه ليس من لوازم العطف تقييد المعطوف بجميع ما قيد به المعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the splitting occur through springs, taking the water poured out as rain and the rivers as its flow; al-Alusi objects that thumma puts the split after the water.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد شقها بالعيون على أن المراد بصب الماء أمطار المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring-water interpretation also fits poorly with crops following both rain and splitting, since 78:14–15 presents rain alone as bringing forth grain.
rows.anchor: لا يلائم قوله تعالى وأنزلنا من المعصرات ماء ثجاجا لنخرج به حبا الآية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A defense says spring water itself comes from rain rather than vapors stored underground; al-Alusi calls the proposal far-fetched and contrived.
rows.anchor: ودفعا بأن ماء العيون من المطر لا من الأبخرة المحتسبة في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired verbs followed by verbal nouns signal an extraordinary divine provision outside familiar custom, supporting the reading that keeps the focus on God's action.
rows.anchor: كما ينبيء منه أرداف الفعلين بالمصدرين فتوسيط فعل المنعم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls are records of deeds; Ibn Jurayj says a person's record is folded at death, then opened on resurrection for judgment according to its contents.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج أنه قال إذا مات الإنسان طويت صحيفته

rows.speaker: مرثد بن وداعة
rows.claim: Mirthad ibn Wadaʿa says the pages are distributed among their owners: on Judgment Day they fly from beneath the Throne, the believer's page falling into his hand in a high garden and the unbeliever's in scorching wind and boiling water; these are not deeds records.
rows.anchor: عن مرثد بن وداعة إذا كان يوم القيامة تطايرت الصحف من تحت العرش

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza, and al-Kisai read nushshirat with a doubled shīn, conveying intensified spreading, many pages, or especially forceful flight.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي نشرت بالتشديد للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage lists apparent differences in Qur'anic statements, including denial that people will ask one another alongside a later description of them asking, and two formulations limiting what prevents belief.
rows.anchor: فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ ولا يتساءلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of verbal variation include wool described once as ṣūf and once as ʿihn, and the ordering of poverty and humiliation in the cited phrase.
rows.anchor: وأما الختلاف فكقوله تعالى ( كالصوف المنفوش )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further alleged inconsistencies include calling the Prophet a father, varying the material from which Adam was created, repetitions in wording and meaning, and explaining that three plus seven days equals ten complete.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ( النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم ) وهو أب لهم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman is reported to have said that the Qur'an contains grammatical irregularities that the Arabs will set right with their tongues.
rows.anchor: وقال عثمان : إن في القرآن لحنا ستقيمه العرب بالسنتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An objection argues that even freedom from all such defects would not establish inimitability, since sermons and poetry show the same feature and the claim scales to short surahs.
rows.anchor: أنا لو سلمنا السلامة من جميع ذلك لكنه ليس بأعجاز إذ هو موجود في كثير من الخطب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A proposed criterion makes the Qur'an miraculous through agreement with reason and subtle meaning; the author rejects it as common among eloquent speech and says it also applies to non-miraculous prophetic speech and the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو موافقته لقضية العقل ودقيق المعنى ورد بأنه معتاد في أكثر كلام البلغاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view locates inimitability in the Qur'an's pre-eternity; the author objects that this would make all divine attributes miraculous and that an unobservable eternal speech cannot be the object of a challenge.
rows.anchor: وقيل إعجازه قدمه وأعترض بأنه يستدعي أن يكون كل من صفاته تعالى كذلك

rows.speaker: الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الأسفراييني والنظام
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini and al-Nazzam say the miracle is that God diverted eloquent Arabs' motives from attempting a rival; al-Murtada instead says their necessary knowledge for competing was removed.
rows.anchor: إعجازه بصرف دواعي بلغاء العرب عن معارضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that the diversion theory makes the miracle the act of diversion rather than the Qur'an itself, contrary to the Muslims' prior consensus.
rows.anchor: أنه يستلزم أن يكون المعجز الصرفة لا القرآن وهو خلاف ما عليه إجماع المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He further argues that if each Arab was diverted individually, producing a like text would be customary for each; ordinary speech is not eloquent, so the theory wrongly entails that the Qur'an itself is not eloquent.
rows.anchor: فلو كان الإعجاز بالصرفة لكانت على خلاف المتعاد بالنسبة إلى كل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl derives from return; deriving it instead from siyāsa, management, as if the interpreter directs speech and places its meaning, is unsound.
rows.anchor: والتأويل من الأول وهو الرجوع والقول بأنه من الأيالة وهي السياسة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats tafsir and taʾwīl as synonymous.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو عبيدة هما بمعنى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says tafsir is broader and more often concerns words and individual expressions in divine books and others, while taʾwīl concerns meanings and whole constructions in divine books specifically.
rows.anchor: الراغب : التفسير أعم وأكثر إستعماله في الألفاظ ومفرداتها

rows.speaker: الماتريدي
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi distinguishes decisive assertion of God's intended meaning as tafsir from preferring one possible meaning without certainty as taʾwīl.
rows.anchor: الماتريدي : التفسير القطع بأن مراد الله تعالى كذا والتأويل ترجيح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another distinction says tafsir depends on transmitted reports whereas taʾwīl depends on reasoned analysis.
rows.anchor: وقيل التفسير ما يتعلق بالرواية والتأويل ما يتعلق بالدراية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the distinction is conventional, earlier definitions do not match current usage: taʾwīl now commonly means sacred allusions and divine insights unveiled to spiritual wayfarers, while tafsir means something else; if based on literal implication, the distinctions should be reconsidered, though every unveiling entails a return and every return an unveiling.
rows.anchor: إذ قد تعارف من غير نكير أن التأويل إشارة قدسية ومعارف سبحانية تنكشف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic interpretation is needed because understanding its legal rulings, the basis of lasting happiness and the straight path, is difficult and requires God's enabling grace.
rows.anchor: فلأن فهم القرآن العظيم المشتمل على الأحكام الشرعية التي هي مدار السعادة الأبدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even eloquent Companions with hearts illuminated by prophecy repeatedly asked the Prophet about matters they had not understood, and sometimes misunderstood God's intent, as Adi ibn Hatim did with the white and black thread; people today need interpretation at least as much.
rows.anchor: كما وقع لعدي بن حاتم في الخيط الأبيض والأسود ولا شك أنا محتاجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses heard God's speech directly, without intermediary but from behind a veil; people hear it from a human reciter's articulated voice, not immediately from God behind that person.
rows.anchor: موسى عليه السلام سمع من الله عزوجل بلا واسطة لكن من وراء حجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sunni formula that the uncreated Qur'an is recited by tongues, heard by ears, kept in hearts, and written in codices means it appears in created manifestations without residing in them, so its pre-eternity remains intact.
rows.anchor: القرآن كلام الله عزوجل غير مخلوق وهو مقروء بألسنتنا مسموع بآذاننا محفوظ في صدورنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eternal's manifestation in a created locus does not compromise its eternity or transcendence and does not entail indwelling, corporealism, or temporal events in God.
rows.anchor: وهذا عين الدليل على أن تجلي القديم في مظهر حادث لا ينافي قدمه وتنزيهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account explains reports that the Qur'an appears as a pale man meeting its companion when the grave opens, and as an adversary against someone who carried it but violated it, or a defender of one who carried and preserved it.
rows.anchor: وعنه يظهر معنى ظهور القرآن في صورة الرجل الشاحب يلقى صاحبه حين ينشق عنه القبر

words: وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ فِىٓ إِمَامٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With this framework, the author dismisses objections made by Ibn Taymiyya, Ibn al-Qayyim, Ibn Qudama, Ibn Qadi al-Jabal, al-Tufi, Abu Nasr, and others as polemical attacks by scholars whose reasoning sometimes erred.
rows.anchor: ورأى أن تشنيع إبن تيمية وإبن القيم وإبن قدامة وإبن قاضي الجبل والطوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He concludes that overlooking the faults of the great scholars is closer to piety and a mark of noble character, rather than answering their attacks in kind.
rows.anchor: على أن العفو أقرب للتقوى والأغضاء مبني الفتوة وعليه الفتوى
